description: F# library for Azure Quantum with quantum-first optimization (Graph Coloring, TSP, MaxCut, Knapsack, Network Flow, Portfolio), Azure Quantum backend integration (IonQ, Rigetti, Quantinuum, Atom Computing), extensible circuit validation, local quantum simulation, QAOA with automatic parameter optimization (Nelder-Mead), OpenQASM 2.0 support, error mitigation techniques (ZNE, PEC, REM), Quantum Random Number Generation (QRNG), and educational quantum algorithms (Grover, QFT, Amplitude Amplification) with cloud backend execution. Native IQuantumBackend integration for IonQ, Rigetti, Quantinuum, Atom Computing, IQM and D-Wave, plus Pasqal neutral-atom analog hardware (via Pulser) and a neutral-atom analog programming model; additional platforms (IBM, Amazon Braket, Google Cirq) are targetable via OpenQASM 2.0 export/import.
releaseNotes:
v1.4.11: GraphOptimization.validateConstraints checks what it claims; 2^n index lists removed from state-vector loops

- CHANGED (false passes): GraphOptimization.validateConstraints returned true for Acyclic without checking anything, and Connected only tested that the PROBLEM graph had at least one edge, so any solution passed both. Acyclic now detects a cycle (a directed cycle for directed edges; any cycle, including a self-loop or parallel edges, otherwise) and Connected checks that the selected edges form one component. Callers can now get false where they previously got true
- CHANGED: DegreeLimit and MinDegree judged the problem graph even when the solution selected edges, so a selection could break either and still pass. The structural constraints (DegreeLimit, MinDegree, Connected, Acyclic) now judge SelectedEdges when present and the problem graph otherwise. MinDegree also counts a node without edges as degree 0; iterating the adjacency map alone passed such nodes unchecked
- CHANGED (memory): Möttönen state preparation kept its rotation angles in a rectangular n x 2^(n-1) table, most of it unused, and at 20 qubits several times the memory of the state being prepared. It now keeps one array per level, 2^n - 1 angles in total, and its inner sums no longer allocate a throwaway list per control pattern. The emitted circuits are bit-identical: 23,360 gates across 1-10 qubits compared against v1.4.10
- CHANGED (memory): several state-vector loops walked the 2^n basis indices through a freshly built F# list, which for a 28-qubit state is several GB before any work starts: HHL's success probability, QuantumState.isNormalized, Measurement.getQubitProbabilities and computeExpectedValue, the QAOA simulator's expected cost and QuantumStateConversion.stateVectorToSparse. They are loops now, summing in the same order, so results are unchanged
- CHANGED: QuantumTspSolver's cost function turned ANY exception into a maximal tour-length penalty, so a decoding bug looked like a bad tour and the parameter optimiser steered around it silently. The catch-all is gone; QuantumTspSolver.solve already turns an exception into an Error, which is where such a bug now surfaces
- CHANGED: MaxCut.completeGraph, cycleGraph and pathGraph indexed their vertex list inside the edge loop (O(i) per access, cubic for the complete graph); they index an array now
- DOCS: the HHL success-probability doc described a condition-number correction that was never applied; the unused parameter is removed and the doc says it reports the measured probability. The four C# option-pricing helpers document numQubits, groverIterations and shots with their valid ranges, and no longer promise a "100x speedup" — the O(1/ε) versus O(1/ε²) advantage is asymptotic and assumes fault-tolerant hardware. Shor.execute's doc had drifted onto executeWith, which now has its own, including the exactness parameter

v1.4.10: Shor is quantum-only; local simulator capacity and speed

BREAKING CHANGES (vs 1.4.9) — the classical period-finding path is gone:
- REMOVED: Shor.PeriodFindingMethod, Shor.findPeriodWith, Shor.executeWithMethod, Shor.executeClassicallyAssisted, Shor.factorClassicallyAssisted, Shor.planPeriodFinding, Shor.ShorPeriodFindingIntent and Shor.ShorPeriodFindingPlan. ShorExecutionIntent loses its Method field and ShorPlan.ExecuteQuantum its method case field
- Why: that path found the period by trial division and then ran a QPE circuit whose phase was built FROM the period it had just found. It could not fail and it demonstrated nothing. Worse, it was not opt-in: Shor.execute asked for PeriodFindingMethod.Quantum and `plan` silently rewrote it to ClassicallyAssisted whenever the circuit did not fit the qubit budget, so callers received a classically computed factorization reported as Success with no field distinguishing it from a quantum one
- CHANGED: Shor.findPeriod and Shor.factor21 ran that path. They now run the genuine circuit — correct, and far slower. Shor.factor21 takes tens of minutes on a local simulator because factoring 21 on a simulated quantum computer takes tens of minutes
- CHANGED: N whose modular-exponentiation circuit exceeds the budget (N ≥ 33 or so at the default 20) now returns a ValidationError naming the shortfall, where it previously returned factors. Raise FSAQ_MAX_CIRCUIT_QUBITS to widen the budget
- CHANGED: Shor rejects QPE.Exactness.Approximate instead of accepting and ignoring it. Only the removed demonstration path ever read it; the quantum path builds an exact inverse QFT
- KEPT: the intent -> plan -> execution pipeline for period finding, which is what lets a non-simulator backend run Shor. Shor.ShorPeriodFindingIntent and Shor.ShorPeriodFindingPlan return with both cases quantum — ExecuteNatively (the backend claims modular-exponentiation QPE as one semantic intent) and ExecuteViaModExpCircuit (the Beauregard circuit, gate by gate). Shor.planPeriodFinding chooses between them per backend, and findPeriodQuantum plans once and reuses the plan across attempts. Previously this pipeline had a single case and it was the classical one, so the genuine path bypassed the abstraction entirely
- FIXED: LocalBackend.SupportsOperation returned true for EVERY QPE intent, including the modular-exponentiation unitary its own ApplyOperation refuses. Planning has to trust that answer, so it now reports by unitary — which is the capability question, whereas TargetQubits is a consequence of the unitary and a wrong count is malformed input rather than a missing capability
- NEW: Shor's period finding is a unified-backend algorithm. QPE.plan lowers a ModularExponentiation unitary to the Beauregard circuit instead of refusing it, so QPE.execute, QPE.executeWithExactness and QPE.plan all accept one where they previously returned "use Shor.estimateModExpPhase". Any gate backend runs the lowered gates; a braid backend compiles them to braids; a backend that claims the intent through SupportsOperation gets ExecuteNatively instead. Nothing needs a private copy of the arithmetic any more
- NEW: Algorithms.ModularExponentiationCircuit exposes that circuit as data — buildModExpQpe (the whole period-finding QPE), buildControlledModularMultiplication (C|y> to C|a*y mod N>), totalQubitsFor and workspaceQubits. It is extracted by running the existing Arithmetic implementation against a recording backend, which is sound because the modular arithmetic performs no measurement, reads no amplitude and branches on nothing but qubit indices and classical constants. There is therefore one implementation, not two, and the extracted circuit cannot drift from the executed one
- CHANGED: Algorithms/QuantumArithmetic.fs now compiles before QPE.fs (it references neither QFT nor QPE, so this is a pure reorder). That ordering was the only reason QPE could not lower modular exponentiation
- CHANGED: Shor.estimateModExpPhase builds its circuit from that same lowering instead of assembling Hadamards, eigenstate preparation, controlled multiplications and an inverse QFT inline. The two constructions agreed, but one circuit with two constructions is how they stop agreeing. Shor's register-width helper likewise delegates to ModularExponentiationCircuit.registerBitsFor, so the module cannot budget for a circuit of one size and then build one of another
- CHANGED: the lowered modular-exponentiation circuit emits its inverse QFT as an AlgorithmOperation.QFT intent instead of expanding it into H and controlled-phase gates. Expanding it dissolved the sub-algorithm into primitives that never reach a backend's intent dispatcher, so a backend able to transform the counting register directly was never asked — algorithm intents worked at the top of a call and then flattened. Backends without a native QFT lower it straight back to the same gates. The swaps stay explicit and appended, because the intent's inverse form applies them before the rotations while period finding needs them after
- FIXED (pre-existing): NoisyLocalBackend initialised as a StateVector while declaring NativeStateType = Mixed. UnifiedBackend.applySequence converts the initial state to the backend's native type before applying anything, and GateBased to Mixed is not implemented, so every applySequence-based algorithm (QPE, QFT, Grover) failed on it there — before the incremental-unsupported fallback that routes such backends to ExecuteToState could fire. It now initialises as |0..0><0..0| in its own representation, and UnifiedBackend.isZeroState recognises a pure-zero density matrix so that fallback's from-|0> check admits it. Single-qubit QPE now runs there end to end. Modular exponentiation still cannot: its Beauregard workspace alone is 2n + 4 qubits, over the density-matrix simulator's 8-qubit cap for any modulus, and it is now refused by that cap's ValidationError rather than by a thrown exception
- FIXED (crash): QPE.execute on a modular-exponentiation unitary THREW on every cloud backend and on the noisy local backend, instead of returning an error. Those backends refuse incremental ApplyOperation, so execution falls back to whole-circuit submission, and that fallback called the single-qubit lowering whose ModularExponentiation arm was a failwith justified as "plan() rejects it first" — an invariant that stopped holding the moment plan() learned to lower modular exponentiation. The same fallback also sized the state as counting + target, leaving the Beauregard circuit no workspace. The arm now returns an error, and plan, execute and the fallback all lower and size through one pair of helpers (lowerToOps, stateWidthFor) so they cannot drift apart again
- NEW: ModularExponentiationCircuit.buildModExpQpeAsGates — the same circuit as buildModExpQpe with its inverse QFT expanded to gates. Whole-circuit submission lowers an op list to a gate circuit and refuses any algorithm intent it meets, so it needs the gates spelled out; planners keep the intent form so a native QFT can compose
- CHANGED: QPE refuses Exactness.Approximate for modular exponentiation, as Shor already did. The lowering builds an exact inverse QFT and the native handlers transform exactly, so Approximate was accepted and silently ignored — the same input got two different answers depending on which entry point it went through
- CHANGED: QPE refuses a TargetQubits that disagrees with the modulus, and a custom EigenVector, for a ModularExponentiation unitary. The lowering derives the register width from the modulus and estimates the phase on |1>, so both inputs were being silently ignored — a correct answer to a different question than the caller asked

- CHANGED: the local simulator's qubit ceiling is derived from available memory instead of a hardcoded 20. LocalSimulator.StateVector.maxQubits reports what the machine can actually hold, bounded at 30 (2^31 amplitudes exceed Array.MaxLength, so 30 is structural, not a policy). LocalBackend.MaxQubits follows it. Override with FSAQ_MAX_QUBITS; StateVector.maxQubitsForAvailableBytes lets a small machine compute what a larger one would allow
- NEW: StateVector.practicalCircuitQubits — a WALL-CLOCK budget (default 20, override FSAQ_MAX_CIRCUIT_QUBITS), deliberately separate from what fits in memory. Algorithms that choose between a genuine circuit and a classical fallback, such as Shor's modular exponentiation, budget against this one. The two limits are not interchangeable: a 26-qubit state fits comfortably and still takes hours to run, because every gate touches all 2^n amplitudes
- NEW: StateVector.stateVectorBytes for callers doing their own capacity planning
- FIXED (admitted work that could not finish): QuantumTspSolver, QaoaExecutionHelpers and ProblemDecomposition admitted a problem on memory capacity alone. Raising the qubit cap from a hardcoded 20 to a memory-derived 28-30 therefore widened what they accept: a 5-city TSP needs 25 qubits, which FITS and does not FINISH, so instead of a fast refusal it put a 25-qubit state through a thousand optimisation iterations. They now ask UnifiedBackend.getRunnableQubits
- NEW: BackendAbstraction.IWallClockLimitedBackend, with UnifiedBackend.getRunnableQubits taking it and MaxQubits together. MaxQubits answers "does it fit", PracticalQubits answers "will it finish", and admission needs both — conflating them is what the bug above was. Simulators implement it (LocalBackend reports StateVector.practicalCircuitQubits); hardware need not, since a shot costs the same there whatever the width. TaskScheduling.QuantumSolver had grown its own copy of this logic as a type test against LocalBackend and now uses the shared helper
- FIXED: the topological backends executed nothing for circuits submitted through any wrapper other than CircuitWrapper — ExecuteToState fell through to an empty result, so QAOA reported a cut of 0 instead of an error
- FIXED: Shor's outer factoring loop treated a period-finding failure as fatal. A base that yields no usable period is exactly what the retry budget exists for, and it now draws a fresh base rather than short-circuiting the run
- FIXED: QuantumTspSolver validates the backend's qubit capacity before building a circuit, and its optimizer iteration budget is configurable rather than fixed
- PERFORMANCE: measurement sampling builds the cumulative distribution once per call rather than once per shot — at 18 qubits and 1000 shots that was 1.9 s and ~2.9 GB of garbage, doubling with every added qubit
- PERFORMANCE: circuit execution applies gates in place instead of allocating a fresh 2^n array per gate, and the single-qubit kernel iterates amplitude pairs directly. Roughly 3.5x faster end to end on wide circuits

v1.4.9: Maintenance release — C# builder fix, property-test suite, formatting
- FIXED: the FSharp.Azure.Quantum.Business.CSharp.dll bundled in 1.4.8 was a stale build against the pre-1.4.8 reference unions, so C# builder calls that touch the now-[<Struct>] types could fail at runtime; it is rebuilt from the current sources. PredictiveModelBuilder (C#) reads ProblemType.Item directly — ProblemType is a struct union since 1.4.8 (the 1.4.8 note saying it stayed a reference union was wrong)
- NEW: tests/FSharp.Azure.Quantum.PropertyTests — FsCheck suite over random circuits: OpenQASM export/import round-trips in every version, exported text is a fixed point, comments never change a parse, invalid circuits are refused, angle expressions parse as written, damaged text yields Error not exceptions; GateTranspiler output for every backend and constraint set simulates to the same state up to global phase, uses only native gates, and is idempotent
- Codebase-wide Fantomas formatting; no functional changes intended

v1.4.8: Maintenance release — fsharp-refactor code clean-up (no functional changes intended)
- CHANGED: ~50 small config/result unions and records are now [<Struct>] (e.g. QFTConfig, NoiseModel, RetryConfig, ConfusionMatrix, PortfolioConfig, AtomCoord, Edge). Source-compatible; binary-incompatible — recompile consumers against 1.4.8
- CHANGED: OracleSpec.And/Or union fields are named (spec1, spec2)
- Ordinal string comparisons, invariant-culture number parsing, use-bindings for disposables, and narrower exception catches throughout
- ProblemType stays a reference union so C# callers can address its cases as nested types

v1.4.7: Correctness release — second-pass audit (silently-wrong-results fixes + dependency updates)

BREAKING CHANGES (vs 1.4.6):
- QuantumClientConfig gained a required Location field (Azure region, e.g. "eastus") and Client.createConfig takes it as a new parameter. QuantumClient now targets the {location}.quantum.azure.com DATA-PLANE endpoint — the previous management.azure.com (ARM) base URL made every live job call fail 401/404 against the quantum-scoped bearer token
- Amplitude encoding (FeatureMap.amplitudeEncoding) prepares the state with amplitude[i] = normalizedFeature[i] (state index = feature index). The previous construction was wrong for most inputs (skipped Gray-code CNOTs, wrong closing control, missing Gray reindexing of the multiplexed-RY angles) — kernels/VQC models trained on amplitude-encoded data should be retrained

FIXED (silently wrong results):
- CRX transpilation was the identity (X commutes with RX, so the RX-CNOT ladder cancelled) — now decomposed as H·CRZ(θ)·H; any transpiled circuit containing CRX was silently missing the gate
- Amplitude amplification's reflection about the prepared state executed A;S0;A† (operator A†·S0·A) instead of A†;S0;A — correct only for self-inverse preparations such as plain Grover's H⊗n
- HHL general (non-diagonal) path maps upper-half QPE register values to NEGATIVE eigenvalues (phase unwrap); a λ < 0 component was previously inverted as phaseScale − |λ|. Phase scale is now 4·maxEig (positive and negative eigenvalues in disjoint phase halves; costs one bit of QPE precision)
- OpenQASM angle formatting in CircuitBuilder.toOpenQASM and QaoaCircuit.toOpenQasm uses InvariantCulture F10 (comma-decimal locales emitted "rx(1,57)" — invalid QASM submitted to paid hardware)
- QuantumClient.GetResultsAsync downloads results from outputDataUri (blob SAS URL) — the job model never inlines outputData, so the previous code could not return results
- SAS blob downloads (job results, Client + JobLifecycle) no longer carry the workspace bearer token: Azure Storage rejected it (401) and the token leaked to the storage host (AuthenticationHandler honors a per-request no-auth marker)
- VQC regression models persist ValueRange (ValueRangeMin/Max in SerializableVQCModel) — reloaded models previously produced affinely-rescaled predictions

FIXED (crashes / robustness):
- Rate-limit exponential backoff overflowed Int32 after ~23 consecutive 429s (Random.Next(min > max) crashed the HTTP pipeline); backoff and job-poll delays now honor cancellation tokens
- Sync ExecuteToState wrappers on the five cloud backends run via Task.Run — no more permanent deadlock when called from a UI thread (WPF/WinForms)
- QAOA multi-start optimization no longer runs two extra objective evaluations (paid quantum jobs) per start for a log line, and only evaluates when a logger is attached
- HttpResponseMessage/JsonDocument disposal in QuantumClient and the D-Wave SAPI backend (socket exhaustion under load)
- Guards: correlation/covariance matrices over return series with no common dates; SMO training with a single sample; confusion matrix with test labels unseen at training; measurement standard deviation NaN from one-ulp negative variance; risk engine rejects SimulationPaths < 2 with a validation error

UPDATED: FSharp.Core 10.1.302, Microsoft.Extensions.Logging 10.0.10, OpenTelemetry 1.17.0, Serilog 4.4.0

v1.4.6: Correctness release — full-library audit (25 critical + ~35 high-severity fixes)

BREAKING CHANGES (vs 1.4.5):
- submitAndWaitForResultsAsync takes a trailing CancellationToken on IonQ/Rigetti/Quantinuum/AtomComputing/Pasqal backends (polling is now cancellable)
- QaoaOptimizer.Optimizer.minimizeWithBounds takes tolerance and maxIterations parameters (config values are now honored; non-convergence returns best-so-far instead of throwing)
- QuantumState gained a MeasurementHistogram case (and QuantumStateType.Sampled) — exhaustive matches must handle or wildcard it
- MitigationTechnique.ReadoutErrorMitigation payload is now CalibrationMatrix option (no fabricated default calibration; missing calibration = pass-through)
- QuantumGraphColoringSolver.solveClassical returns Result instead of throwing when colors run out
- constraintSolver's searchSpace now means NUMBER OF VARIABLES (matching forSudokuStyle/forNQueens); numVariables × log2(domainSize) ≤ 16 qubits is enforced with a clear error
- Knapsack/set-cover/drug-discovery QUBOs use slack variables for inequality constraints (NumVariables grew; decoders unchanged for item bits)
- findCheapestBackend/recommendCostOptimization exclude subscription-priced backends (Quantinuum has no per-job USD price); an all-subscription backend list returns an Error / no recommendation
- Business classification/regression builders REJECT feature counts above the qubit cap (8 binary / 5 predictive) with a clear error instead of failing every epoch (1.4.5) or silently truncating; reduce dimensionality first
- MitigatedResult gained CorrectionApplied: false means the histogram passed through uncorrected (readout mitigation selected without calibration data)

NEW: Wide cloud hardware support
- QuantumState.MeasurementHistogram: sampled results with NO qubit-count limit (at most `shots` entries regardless of width)
- Cloud result tiering everywhere (Braket + Azure backends): dense state ≤ 20 qubits, sparse state 21-31, measurement histogram beyond — Quantinuum H2 (56q), Rigetti Ankaa (~84q), IonQ Forte (36q) results are now usable (previously crashed above 20)

HIGH-severity fixes (selection):
- IonQ result parser accepts the documented Azure probability-histogram format (decimal state keys); live jobs no longer error
- OpenQASM export defines rxx/ryy/rzz inline where qelib1/stdgates lack them; importer accepts the definitions
- VQC gradients apply the chain rule (parameter-shift on circuit expectations × analytic loss derivative) — was a biased finite difference of the loss
- VQC model serialization stores PauliFeatureMap/TwoLocal configuration losslessly (saveVQCModelWithConfigAsync); AutoML train/validation split is seeded-shuffled
- Parametric VaR honors the requested confidence for Student-t/log-normal; Historical redirects to the empirical function; Asian options priced via the exact geometric-average distribution (was silently European)
- Network-flow conservation penalty de-doubled and solutions validated (conservation/supply/demand) before selection; graph-coloring fixed colors enforced; scheduling objective (incl. MinimizeLateness) actually honored
- Portfolio: negative-return zero-risk assets no longer rank first; quantum decode respects Min/MaxHolding; KnapsackBuilder solveClassicalDP is genuine dynamic programming
- Shor draws a fresh random base per retry (N=33-style permanent failures fixed; gcd hits return the factor immediately)
- QRNG local path uses a cryptographic RNG and documentation states it is CSPRNG, not quantum, randomness
- Molecular CSV labels stay aligned; unlabeled drug screening errors instead of reporting every candidate as a hit; malformed SMILES fail at parse time
- Cost recommendations exclude subscription-priced backends (Quantinuum HQC no longer 'cheapest' at $0); QAOA optimizer non-convergence returns best-so-far
- Density-matrix simulator handles Reset/Barrier/Conditional with exact channels; strategy selection no longer allocates a 2^n×2^n placeholder (34 GB at 16 qubits)

v1.4.6 critical fixes (earlier batch):
- FIXED: Circuit adjoint (CircuitBuilder.reverse) now reverses gate order — corrects amplitude amplification reflections and quantum Monte Carlo Grover operators
- FIXED: Multi-controlled X/Z decomposition for 3+ controls (correct ancilla-free recursion; the old "borrowed ancilla" ladder computed the wrong predicate) — affects Grover 4+ qubits and HHL eigenvalue inversion
- FIXED: QUBO -> Ising conversion (fromQubo/fromQuboSparse) now includes cross-term linear contributions, and QuboExtraction is its exact inverse (D-Wave path optimized a corrupted objective before)
- FIXED: Trotter-Suzuki Pauli decomposition qubit ordering (was bit-reversed vs circuit synthesis) and diagonal decomposition (correct I/Z expansion via Walsh-Hadamard transform); HHL controlled-evolution gate order; controlled evolution of identity terms emits the control phase
- FIXED: Zero-noise extrapolation scaled circuits executed in reverse gate order
- FIXED: Budget checks no longer skip the monthly limit when a daily warning fires
- FIXED: Task scheduling — resource capacity encoded with non-negative overload penalties (equality penalty rewarded infeasible schedules); decoded schedules re-validated classically (one-hot, dependencies, resource capacity) with earliest-slot one-hot repair
- FIXED: Grover constraint solver — searchSpace is the number of variables (matching forSudokuStyle/forNQueens), with a 16-qubit feasibility guard; mixed-radix decode no longer overflows
- FIXED: Graph coloring greedy solver returns Result instead of throwing when colors run out (HybridSolver propagates)
- FIXED: ML — amplitude-encoding Walsh-Hadamard butterfly (wrong state for 3+ qubits), 2-class VQC prediction (always returned first class), anomaly detection rebuilt on kernel centroid distance (one-class SVM was degenerate and could never learn); model loaders validate model kind (wrong-kind files no longer load as VQC-regression with null parameters)
- FIXED: Invariant-culture number parsing in chemistry and market data (comma-decimal locales silently lost elements/atoms/returns)
- FIXED: Parametric Expected Shortfall no longer overstated by factor z (~2.33x at 99%); risk engine errors on missing/malformed data instead of fabricating zeros or mock returns
- FIXED: D-Wave direct backend speaks the documented SAPI v2 qp wire format (base64 lin/quad against solver topology; correct submit/poll/answer decoding); problems off the hardware graph error explicitly (minor-embedding not implemented)
- NOTE: P(theta) transpiles to RZ(theta) on backends without a native phase gate (equal up to global phase)

v1.4.3: Neutral-atom analog mode, CUDA-Q-style primitives, and new backends
- NEW: Neutral-atom (Rydberg) analog programming - NeutralAtom module Trotterizes an analog program to gates; PasqalBackend (RydbergProgram -> Pulser JSON -> Azure Quantum) and QueraBackend (RydbergProgram -> Braket AHS JSON)
- NEW: CUDA-Q-style execution primitives (Primitives: sample/observe/run/getState) over IQuantumBackend, plus CudaQBridge
- NEW: ADAPT-VQE and ADAPT-QAOA adaptive-ansatz algorithms (AdaptVqe, AdaptQaoa)
- NEW: IQM gate backend (IqmBackend)
- NEW: Density-matrix noisy simulator backend (NoisyBackend)
- NEW: Emulate-target mode (Emulation) - transpile, validate, then run locally for a cloud target
- NEW: Companion FSharp.Azure.Quantum.Braket package isolates the AWS SDK dependency (QuEra neutral-atom analog and Braket gate QPUs)
- IMPROVED: Business builders and ML model serialization refactors

v1.4.2: Compilation/hardware tooling and weighted MAX-SAT
- NEW: QubitRouting - inserts SWAPs so two-qubit gates respect device connectivity (CouplingMap: grid/linear/fromPairs); tracks logical-to-physical qubit permutation
- NEW: CloudBackends.Factory.createRigettiRouted - Rigetti backend that auto-routes circuits for a device coupling map
- NEW: QirEmitter - emit circuits as QIR base-profile textual LLVM IR for Azure Quantum submission
- NEW: ResourceEstimation - logical (qubits/gates/T-count/depth) and physical (surface-code) resource estimates
- NEW: NoiseModel - DeviceNoiseProfile with noise-aware routing (routeNoiseAware) and success-probability estimation
- NEW: Weighted MAX-SAT - per-clause weights in QuantumSatSolver (clause / weightedClause); solution reports SatisfiedWeight/TotalWeight
- IMPROVED: AutoML returns a typed TrainedModel discriminated union instead of obj (no unboxing in predict)
- IMPROVED: Connected-component decomposition now unions sub-solutions for Vertex Cover and Maximum Matching
- IMPROVED: Knapsack builder shares the solver item type (no duplicate record or field mapping)

v1.4.1: Dependency updates
- UPDATED: Azure.Identity 1.13.1 to 1.21.0
- UPDATED: FSharp.Core to 10.1.301
- UPDATED: Microsoft.Extensions.Logging to 10.0.9, Serilog to 4.3.1
- UPDATED: OpenTelemetry to 1.16.0 (Exporter.Console 1.16.0, Instrumentation.Http 1.15.1)

v1.3.10: Async backend refactoring
- NEW: Task-based async APIs on IQuantumBackend (ExecuteToStateAsync, ApplyOperationAsync) with CancellationToken
- NEW: Async QAOA execution helpers (executeQaoaCircuitAsync, executeQaoaWithGridSearchAsync, executeWithBudgetAsync)
- NEW: Async ML pipeline (computeKernelAsync, computeKernelMatrixAsync, predictAsync, evaluateAsync)
- NEW: Cloud backend factory (CloudBackendFactory) for Rigetti, IonQ, Quantinuum, AtomComputing
- NEW: UnifiedBackend async helpers (applySequenceAsync, applyWithConversionAsync)
- NEW: OpenQASM export async (exportToFileAsync, exportToFileWithConfigAsync)
